name: ORCID
tagline: A persistent digital identifier for researchers to distinguish themselves and connect with their professional activities across disciplines, borders, and time
sdg_alignment: SDG 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
dependency_risks: Reliance on institutional subscriptions and public funding
academic_citations: Haak, L. L., et al. (2012). ORCID: a system to uniquely identify researchers. Research Trends, 31, 6-7.
Fenner, M., et al. (2014). A data citation roadmap for scholarly data repositories. bioRxiv, 097196.
policy_outcomes: Adoption by major research funders (NIH, NSF, Horizon Europe)
Integration into institutional research information systems
Mandated use in grant applications by major funding agencies
documented_limitations: Adoption varies by discipline and geography
failure_modes: Duplicate ORCID records created by users
Low adoption in some developing regions
curation_criteria: Community-driven with peer review for integrations; governed by ORCID Board of Directors representing stakeholder organizations
contributor_governance: Open contribution model with community input; governance through member organizations and community working groups
disparity_tracking: Monitoring adoption disparities across geographic regions and research disciplines; efforts to increase adoption in underrepresented regions
community_ownership: Member-based governance with input from research institutions, funders, and publishers
political_relevance_summary: ORCID addresses the challenge of persistent researcher identification, enabling transparent attribution of research outputs that inform policy. Its civic relevance is indirect but foundational to research integrity.

movement_building_utility.notes: ORCID provides foundational data infrastructure, standards, or platforms that other civic technology efforts build upon.

generalizability_notes: High generalizability. ORCID is open source and already deployed across multiple countries/jurisdictions, making replication straightforward for other contexts.
